newsitem.title: USA: Pennzoil posts profit for fourth quarter.
newsitem.headline: Pennzoil posts profit for fourth quarter.

text.p: Pennzoil Co. reported a fourth-quarter profit vs. a year-ago loss Wednesday due to higher oil and natural gas prices and lower costs.

The maker of Pennzoil motor oil posted net income of $28.5 million, or 61 cents a share, for the fourth quarter, compared with a loss of $27.8 million, or 60 cents a share, in the same period a year ago.
Revenues hit $609.2 million vs. $608 million in the year-ago quarter, the Houston-based company said.

For the year, Pennzoil made $133.9 million in profits, or $2.88 a share, compared with a loss of $305.1 million, or $6.60 per share, in 1995. Revenues hit $2.486 billion vs. $2.489 billion a year ago.

The 1996 results included $33 million in gains primarily from the sale of various assets, while 1995 earnings were hit by $297 million in after-tax charges for adoption of a new accounting standard and other one-time items.
"In 1996, Pennzoil made considerable progress toward improving its financial and operating performance," company Chairman James Pate said in a statement.
Pate said the company cut general and administrative costs by more than $80 million, exceeding its goal of trimming such costs by $75 million.
Operating income increased primarily in 1996 mainly due to increase natural gas and crude oil prices and reduced production costs, Pennzoil said.
The cost of producing a barrel of oil dropped to $4.41 per barrel from $5.09 in 1995. Pennzoil stock rose 37.5 cents to $62.375 on the New York Stock Exchange.
